answer: A fable about a walnut seller shows the trick: one stall is cheap, but each extra stall run by the same hands costs far more, and the deposit stays locked until the stall has served honestly for a season. Apply that to agents: a new pseudonym must lock a deposit that escalates with every identity funded from the same source, released only after sustained honest work. A lone agent passes easily, while a sockpuppet farm burns its budget fast, and the locked deposits act as a beacon marking which identities have real skin in the game.
